items.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
items.snippet: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
items.snippet: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.

items.title: Proximal Ventures raises debut fund to back startups bringing AI to drug development
items.snippet: Former SignalFire investor Sahir Raoof raises $27.5 million for new fund targeting AI in pharma.

items.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
items.snippet: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.

items.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
items.snippet: The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”

items.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
items.snippet: PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to answer a fundamental question about quantum computing that scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
items.snippet: OpenAI is looking to make ChatGPT a more robust consumer discovery engine, and a host of new features seek to empower businesses to help it do that.

items.title: Pixel Tag, Google's $30 Android-ready answer to Apple's AirTag, is now available

items.title: Apple's Claris Testing 'Harbor' App for Local AI on Macs
items.snippet: Apple's Claris subsidiary is testing an app called Harbor , which turns Apple silicon Macs into a private AI server. Harbor works with a single Apple silicon Mac, but it also supports connecting multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory for larger models. Apple added RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 with macOS Tahoe 26.2, making clustering faster. Harbor detects devices connected over Thunderbolt 5 and lets users browse for, download, and load open-weight models. It's described as an easy-to-use app with no manual configuration required. Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware

items.title: The Original iPod Went on Sale 25 Years Ago Today
items.snippet: Apple's original iPod went on sale 25 years ago today, on November 10, 2001. The $399 music player initially worked only with a Mac, but it went on to become one of Apple's most significant products and helped the company expand beyond the computer business. Steve Jobs had unveiled the first iPod just over two weeks earlier, on October 23, at a small press event in the Town Hall auditorium at Apple's Infinite Loop headquarters. Advertised as offering "1,000 songs in your pocket," the device combined a 5GB hard drive with a monochrome LCD display, a mechanical scroll wheel, and up to 10 hours of battery life. items.title: Apple Maps Could Factor Parking Into Your Arrival Time
items.snippet: Apple may be working on a way for Maps arrival estimates that account for parking as well as the walk to your destination, according to findings shared by code explorer pdfu . A new "TimeToPark" flag in the iOS 27.3 beta apparently allows the system to measure time spent near a destination before parking, plus walking time afterwards. The measurements use background location and motion data, with results saved per trip and grouped by weekday and hour. However, pdfu says the feature can only be enabled on internal installations, and no Maps feature uses the data yet. In other words, watch this space – parking-aware ETAs could yet become a thing. items.snippet: Macworld With the MacBook Pro with PROLED Display, Apple returned the Apple logo to its former glory, switching from shiny aluminum to one that lights up and glows again. And it’s got a new trick: Turn up the display brightness, and the logo gets brighter, too. Turn down the display brightness, and the logo dims. However, since the brightness controls on the display and logo are linked, the only way to turn the brightness on the logo all the way down is to also turn off the display. And sadly, Apple did not include a system setting control for the logo, so you can’t turn it off by simply flicking a switch. But you can turn it off through Terminal, Apple’s command line interface for the Mac.

items.title: Altar II Keyboard on Kickstarter
items.snippet: Electronic Materials Office is the brainchild of Andrew Emerson. Back in 2023 he launched the Altar I, a rather distinctive mechanical keyboard. Much thinner than most, very opinionated in its industrial design and keycap typography. I got one and I don’t regret it, but there was too much I didn’t like about it, so it’s mostly sat in a drawer. Today on Kickstarter Emerson/EMO has launched a campaign for the Altar II. Same cool aesthetic, but with improvements that address everything I didn’t like about the Altar I. The Altar II has all new switches. items.title: Steven Levy on John Ternus
items.snippet: Steven Levy at Wired, in a terrific post-event follow-up to his exclusive early look at the new MacBook Pros ( News+ link ): I first met Ternus in 2015, when I spent a day with him at Apple’s Input Design Lab, a testing facility in Cupertino. items.title: OurCal
items.snippet: My thanks to OurCal for sponsoring last week at DF. You ever have a discussion that starts with “I didn’t see you put that on the calendar”? Could be with your colleagues, could be with your family. But the problem is familiar: Shared calendars solved scheduling, not communication. OurCal connects any calendar, new or existing, to a group chat. Changes post there automatically, so nobody misses them. Because it’s a messenger, they made everything end-to-end encrypted, certified by France’s cybersecurity agency. OurCal is native SwiftUI across Apple’s platforms, and the App Store just featured it in “Great apps on iPhone Duo”. They’ve got an Android app too, but they’re an Apple-first company

items.title: Safari 27.3 Adds Support for Global Privacy Control
items.snippet: Nick Heer, Pixel Envy: There are a whole bunch of features and fixes coming to Safari with Apple’s OS 27.3 update. One that is not in the beta release notes but appears nevertheless is support for Global Privacy Control . This new standard is effectively a replacement for Do Not Track with legal muscle that should permit you to indicate your tracking preference one time and then, theoretically, never again see a cookie consent banner. ★

items.title: How to disable incoming IP addresses without DNs resolution in Apache using Fail2Ban without HostnameLookups?
items.snippet:
<p>To block crawlers without a DNS-entry, a simple solution sets <code>HostnameLookups On</code> in the apache configuration, then creates a filter <code>apache-numeric-ip.conf</code> :</p>
<pre class="lang-none prettyprint-override"><code>[Definition]
failregex = ^<ADDR>.*$
</code></pre>
<p>And adds it to <code>jail.local</code>:</p>
<pre class="lang-none prettyprint-override"><code>[apache-numeric-ip]
enabled = true
filter = apache-numeric-ip
logpath = /var/log/apache2/access.log
maxretry = 5
findtime = 5m
bantime = 8h
</code></pre&g
